title: CFP: BISA 2026: 20th Anniversary Conference
content:
Call for Papers

BISA 2026: 20th Anniversary Conference, Bristol

British and Irish Sound Archives (BISA) invites proposals for presentations at
this year’s BISA conference, which will be held at Bristol on Thursday 14 and
Friday 15 May 2026.

The two-day conference will feature presentations, practical sessions and
collaborative discussions, as well as the BISA Annual General Meeting.

We welcome proposals on any aspect of working in the sound heritage field. As
we will be celebrating our 20th anniversary in 2026, we’re interested in hearing
from archivists, engineers, researchers and other sound archives and creative
practitioners interested in reflecting on changes to practice, technology, and
research use that have taken place over the last two decades.

Previous delegates have also expressed an interest in the following aspects of
sound archive work and research: digitisation and digital preservation;
cataloguing; access and re-use; copyright and data protection; fundraising and
advocacy; and AI.

Please send a description of the presentation you propose, in no more than 300
words, to british.irish.sound.archive@gmail.com by 5pm on Friday 13 February.

title: Call for Papers: transfer – Zeitschrift für Provenienzforschung und Sammlungsgeschichte / Journal for Provenance Research and the History of Collection Vol. 6 (2027), No. 1
content:
The online journal transfer is an academic publication platform in the area of provenance research and the history of collection as well as adjacent fields of investigation, like art market studies, reception history, cultural sociology, or legal history. Issues are published semi-annually and exclusively online in Diamond Open Access. Research articles and research reports, to be submitted in English or German, are subject to a double-blind peer-review. All submissions undergo an internal evaluation by the editors supported by the advisory board and receive professional copy-editing before publication. The journal is based at the Research Centre for Provenance Research, Art and Cultural Property Law at the University of Bonn and at the Leipzig Museum of Fine Arts. transfer receives funding from the German Research Foundation (DFG). Webhosting is provided by our partner institution Heidelberg University Library via arthistoricum.net.

Website: https://ahnp.ub.uni-heidelberg.de/journals/transfer/index

Editors: Felicity Bodenstein, Ulrike Saß & Christoph Zuschlag

Managing Editor: Florian Schönfuß

title: G.L.A.M.* Bookworms Book Club
content:
The next G.L.A.M.* Bookworms Book Club discussion via Zoom is on Wednesday, Dec. 9, at 7pm (ET).

We’ll be discussing THE CLOISTERS by Katy Hays:

A recent graduate takes a research job at the Metropolitan Museum of Art’s secluded branch called The Cloisters and becomes entangled in a secretive group of researchers studying tarot’s power to predict death, leading to obsession, manipulation, and a dangerous unraveling of truth and fate.

All are welcome to join the discussion! RSVP for the Zoom link, or if you have any questions: info@wolfsonarchives.org.

This book club is sponsored by Miami Dade College’s Lynn and Louis Wolfson II Florida Moving Image Archives.

content:

title: CFP: Transatlantic Slavery and the Archive Conference, 2027
content:
The National Archives is pleased to announce details of the conference, Transatlantic Slavery and the Archive. The conference is one of the outputs of PASSAGE (Partnership for Atlantic Slavery, Scholarship, Archiving and Global Exchange), which is funded by the Lloyd’s Register Foundation.Conference dates

21–22 June, 2027Venue
The National Archives, KewDeadline for submissions
17.00 (GMT/UTC+0) on Monday 14 December 2026

Histories of transatlantic slavery have long been shaped by the archive. This has led researchers to confront the fact that records of transatlantic slavery were overwhelmingly written by or for enslavers.

Influential critiques by Michel-Rolph Trouillot (Silencing the Past, 1995) and Saidiya Hartman (Scenes of Subjection, 1997; ‘Venus in Two Acts’, 2008) have highlighted the relationship between archival production, power, violence and historical silence. They have shown how the lives of enslaved people are often fragmented, obscured, or wholly absent from the documentary record.

title: Call for Submissions: “Biz of Digital” Column in Upcoming Issues of Against the Grain
content:
Against the Grain is seeking submissions for our “Biz of Digital” column! Biz of Digital features articles by working librarians and information professionals on digital collections, digital repositories, digital scholarship, data services, and technology. Its audience is librarians in all types of libraries and vendors of products, services, and systems that support library digital services. Its focus is on current practices, techniques, processes, and information on events in the field. Against the Grain is a down-to-earth, practice-orientated library journal.
Tell us about your interesting projects, new initiatives, successes, failures and lessons learned about:

*   Digitization and preservation
*   Digital repositories
*   Digital scholarship
*   Copyright and licensing
*   Systems and emerging technologies
*   Research data services
*   Data discovery
*   Data science and data visualization
*   AI in libraries
*   Metadata and standards
*   Research integrity
*   Digital accessibility and usability

title: CFP: MATTER & MEMORY: The Preservation of Cultural and Material Heritage
content:
SESSION CALL:

MATTER & MEMORY: The Preservation of Cultural and Material Heritage

PORTO

Conference: Heritages 2027
Dates: 16-18, June, 2027
Abstracts due: 10 Dec, 2026

https://amps-research.com/porto-ipca-themes/

SESSION CALL

Cultural heritage is continually interpreted, preserved and transformed through changing historical, social and artistic contexts. This session builds on this and examines how societies construct, transmit and reassess cultural memory through objects, monuments, artworks, archives and historic environments. We argue that within history and art history, such processes raise important questions about authenticity, authorship, representation and the changing meanings attached to cultural artefacts and sites.

Contributions might consider contemporary interventions in historic buildings, restoration and reconstruction, digital technologies, museum practices, or new approaches to documenting and interpreting the past.
